reason: Forfeiture of the whole Security Deposit on early termination. Whether it is a penalty is a s.74 question, not ss.27-28. (The cross-reference to 'Article III' for the deposit appears to be an error: the deposit is in Article VI.)
The Lessor limits how it lets the rest of its own premises, and only during the lease. A restriction on dealing with its property, not a restraint on anyone's trade.

The claim is 'deemed waived and abandoned' and the other party 'discharged' if arbitration is not started within 90 days of the dispute arising. Extinguishes the right on expiry of a period; void, and the 3-year period under the Limitation Act applies (s.43 A&C Act).

Expressly subject to the arbitration clause, and names Coimbatore, where the premises are. Those courts have jurisdiction anyway (Hakam Singh, A.B.C. Laminart). The costs sentence does not touch s.28.
Lock-in: the Lessee pays rent for the full 2 years if it leaves earlier, recoverable from the deposit. Whether that is a penalty is a s.74 question.
A post-lease non-compete (3 years after vacating, Sector 16 and adjoining sectors). No goodwill sold. Void however limited in time and area.
A notice step so the Lessor can arrange repairs. No consequence is attached to late notice, so no right is lost.

Bars every suit, arbitration or other proceeding for loss of or damage to the Lessee's goods, and waives the right to bring them. An absolute restriction for that class of claims; void to that extent. Clause 25 (no responsibility for goods) is a liability exclusion and outside scope; it is 25A's bar on proceedings that offends.
Limits a suit for refund of the deposit to 6 months from handover, against 3 years under the Limitation Act (Art. 55 or 113). Void under s.28(a).
Holding over: deemed unauthorised occupation and 'penal interest' of Rs. 1,00,000 per day. Whether that is a penalty is a s.74 question.

Operates only during the Lease Term but restrains the Lessee from taking other premises anywhere in Udyog Vihar Phases I-V for an online travel business, not just use of these premises. In-term, but elsewhere, and the landlord's interest is not apparent from the deed. Refer.
Gurgaon courts, and the premises are in Udyog Vihar, Gurgaon. Those courts have jurisdiction over the property. There is no arbitration clause to read it with.
Restraint on debt-collection business in Udyog Vihar for 1 year after the Initial Term or earlier termination. Post-lease; no goodwill sold. Void.

The build-out is 'deemed accepted as complete and in conformity with Schedule II' unless defects are notified in 15 days. That deeming takes away the claim for defective build-out (cl. 7(xv)) on expiry of a period, so it is void under s.28(b). The notice step alone would be valid; the deeming words are what is void. Worth discussing (deemed-acceptance clauses).
Lessors 'released and discharged' from refund and cure-cost claims unless notified within 30 days of vacating. Discharge on expiry of a period; void.

Exclusive jurisdiction to New Delhi for premises in Gurgaon. Delhi courts may have jurisdiction over money claims (the Lessee's registered office is there), but not over the property. Whether this leaves a competent court for every claim depends on facts outside the text. Refer.
The Lessor will not let adjoining SEZ land to a competing user during the lease. A restriction on how the Lessor deals with its own property, in-term only.

Claims for return of the bank guarantee or the rebate are 'forfeited' and the Lessor 'discharged' unless lodged within 90 days of the guarantee's expiry. Extinguishment on expiry of a period. This is a term of the lease between the parties, not the bank's guarantee, so Exception 3 does not apply.
A binding agreement to refer disputes to a three-member tribunal under the 1996 Act. Saved by Exception 1. The negotiation period before reference is not a time bar.
The claim for excess rent is 'deemed waived' and the Lessor 'discharged' unless made within 60 days of handover. Void under s.28(b).
Limits what the premises may be used for during the Lease Period. The Lessee may run any business elsewhere.

Arbitration with seat at Chennai, and the competent courts of Chennai, where the premises are. Both are valid. The 'only' courts sentence and the arbitration sentence sit together; the courts' role is supervisory.
Excludes consequential loss and caps the Lessee's liability. This limits what is recoverable, not the right to go to court; not a s.28 clause.

Maintenance bills raised by the Lessor's nominee are 'deemed accepted as correct and binding' unless disputed in 30 days. After that the Lessee cannot challenge the bill, so the right is extinguished on expiry of a period. Void to that extent. Same question as PO-14 and PO-66.
Lock-in: on early termination the Lessor may deduct the entire rent for the lock-in from the deposits. A s.74 question.
Civil courts at Gurgaon and the Punjab and Haryana High Court; the premises are in DLF City, Gurgaon. Courts that have jurisdiction anyway.

The Lessor's own determination of super built-up area is 'final, conclusive and binding' and, notwithstanding cl. 22, cannot be questioned in any court or authority. One party decides, and every forum is shut out. Not an independent expert, so not the BP-7 'refer' case. Void.
The Lessors will not let other units in the Building to the Lessee's competitors during the Initial Term. Restriction on dealing with property, in-term.
Limits the Lessee's remedy for breach of 11A to damages, with no specific performance or injunction. The court is still open for damages; this is a remedies question, not s.28.
Binding arbitration by a sole arbitrator appointed by mutual consent under the 1996 Act. Saved by Exception 1. (The definitions refer to 'Clause 27.1' for Dispute; it should be 26.1.)
Any claim not referred to arbitration within 6 months of arising is 'barred'. Limits the time to enforce rights to less than the 3-year period. Void under s.28(a).
The 'Non-Compete Period' is defined as 2 years starting when the Term ends, so this is a post-lease restraint (Park and 3 km radius). No goodwill sold. Void.
Notice within 7 days so the Lessor can lodge warranty claims. No consequence attached; no right lost.

Disputes about maintenance services and charges may not go to arbitration or to any court, and the Lessor's decision is final. Overrides cl. 18(d) and leaves no forum for that class of claims. Void to that extent.
Exclusion of the Lessor's liability for certain losses. Limits recovery, not access to court.

The Lessor's computation of rent escalation and Fit-Out Fees is final, and no dispute about it may go to arbitration or to any court, notwithstanding cl. 18(b). No forum for that class of claims. Void to that extent.
Three years from when the amount fell due, the same as Art. 52 (rent) and Art. 55/113 (deposit). Not shorter than the statutory period, so not void, though it gives no extra time either.
Bars any suit, arbitration or proceeding about deductions from the IFRSD for damage, and waives the right. An absolute restriction for that class of claims; void to that extent.
In-term only, but restrains the Lessee from taking any other office space anywhere in NOIDA for its business. A restraint on business elsewhere, with no apparent landlord interest. Refer.
Requires at least 15 days' notice before starting arbitration. A minimum notice, not a deadline: nothing is lost by giving it late, the claim just waits 15 days.
The Lessee is 'released and discharged' from damage claims unless the Lessor notifies them within 30 days of handover. Discharge on expiry of a period. Section 28 protects the Lessor as well.

The Lessor's computation is binding 'without prejudice to the right of the LESSEE to refer any dispute ... to arbitration under Article XXII'. The forum is preserved; this only says the figure is payable pending a dispute.
The Lessor's covenant not to let to SAP competitors runs during the term and for a year after it. During the term it is valid; the post-term year is the doubtful part. Refer.
Interest on late payment and the right to cut off services after notice. Neither limits recourse to courts. Outside ss.27-28.
User clause: premises only as an office. Restricts use of the landlord's property, not the tenant's trade elsewhere.
Notice of billing discrepancies within 15 days so the Lessor can verify. No deeming and no loss of rights.
12 months after expiry or termination, Guindy Industrial Estate. Post-lease restraint; no goodwill. Void.

An independent chartered surveyor, jointly nominated, whose certificate on area is final and binding. An agreed way of fixing a fact; courts not expressly excluded and cl. 12.E arbitration remains. Refer, per the BP-7 approach. (Note: the deed has two sub-clauses lettered J; this is the first.)

Area is fixed by a surveyor nominated by the Lessor alone, and his determination cannot be questioned before the cl. 18 tribunal 'or before any court'. A party's nominee plus an express exclusion of every forum. Void.

The Lessor sold the goodwill of its storage business to the Lessee and restrains itself within Mundra Taluka for as long as the buyer carries on a like business. All three conditions of Exception 1 are met; reasonableness of the limits is for the court. Refer.
Pre-determined damages for holding over at 5% of monthly rent per day. A s.74 question. The renewal terms raise nothing under ss.27-28.
Two years after the Term ends, within the NOIDA notified area. Post-lease restraint; no goodwill. Void.
Fifteen days' notice before changing the layout. An ordinary step under the contract; says nothing about claims or courts.
Notwithstanding cl. 39, no arbitration, suit or proceeding over the cafeteria, and the Lessor's decision is final. No forum for that class of claims. Void to that extent.
Mutual exclusion of indirect and consequential loss. Limits recovery, not access to court.
A claim 'shall stand extinguished' if the Notice of Dispute is not issued within 6 months of the cause of action. Extinguishment on expiry of a period; void.

The Lessor may not bring any suit, arbitration or proceeding for rent arrears; its only remedy is adjustment against the deposit. An absolute restriction on enforcing that right through the courts or arbitration, even where arrears exceed the deposit. Void to that extent. Section 28 protects the landlord too.
Forfeiture of the initial deposit, processing fee and part of the development charges on surrender. A s.74 question.

The cost fixed by the Lessor 'cannot be questioned in any Court of law'. One party decides, and courts are excluded, but arbitration is not: cl. 35 sends 'any question of dispute or difference' to an arbitrator. If cl. 35 reaches this cost, a forum remains and the clause is not an absolute bar; if it does not, it is void. Needs reading of the two together. Refer.

Read as a whole this is a binding agreement to arbitrate ('shall be referred'). The opening words, that the lessee shall not raise disputes during the lease, are immediately qualified by 'if at all raised ... referred to an arbitrator', so they do not leave the lessee without a forum. Saved by Exception 1. Appointment by the Government of Tamil Nadu, which controls SIPCOT, is open to challenge under Perkins Eastman and CORE (and s.12(5)), but that goes to appointment, not s.28. Worth discussing.

Only the courts of the City of Chennai, for a plot at Siruseri in Kancheepuram district. Chennai courts likely have jurisdiction over money claims (SIPCOT's office), but not over the property itself. Refer.
18 months after the Lease Term, within the Instronics Estate. Post-lease restraint; no goodwill. Void.

Force majeure with a 7-day notice condition. Late notice means the party cannot rely on the force majeure excuse; it does not extinguish any right to sue or discharge any liability on the expiry of a period. Valid.
Three years from when the sum fell due, the same as the Limitation Act period for money claims. Not shorter, so not void.

A binding arbitration agreement. Part D(i) says the Delhi Rent Control Act applies, but at Rs. 11,000 a month the premises fall outside it (s.3(c) of that Act excludes premises let at over Rs. 3,500 a month), and parties cannot confer rent-control jurisdiction by agreement. The tenancy is under the Transfer of Property Act, so arbitrable (Vidya Drolia). Valid. If you prefer to keep every 'rent control' clause as refer, mark refer; I would discuss this.

The Lessors' statement of charges is 'deemed to be correct and accepted' unless disputed within 15 days. That takes away the right to dispute the charge on expiry of a period. Void to that extent. Same question as PO-14 and PO-24.
User clause: only as a corporate office. Restricts use of these premises, not the Lessee's trade elsewhere.

Goodwill of the cafeteria business is sold and the restraint lasts as long as the buyer carries on the business, but the area is 'anywhere in India'. That is not a 'specified local limit', so Exception 1 does not apply. Void.
Courts in Bangalore, where the premises are (Koramangala). Courts with jurisdiction anyway.
No suit more than 1 year after the breach, against 3 years under Art. 55. Shortens the time to sue; void.
